blocks.text: Charles Darwin was an English scientist. In 1831 he travelled as a naturalist on a scientific expedition aboard His Majesty's Ship Beagle, a five-year voyage around the world.

blocks.alt: World map with orange land and pale blue sea. A dark blue line with arrowheads traces the Beagle's route from Plymouth south past Tenerife and Cape Verde to Rio de Janeiro, round South America by the Falkland Islands, up the west coast to Galapagos and off to the west; it returns from the east past Sydney, Hobart, Mauritius and Cape Town, back across the Atlantic and north to Plymouth. Red dots mark stops; Plymouth and Galapagos are labelled in pink, the other eight in dark blue.
blocks.caption: Figure 24.1: Main stops in the route of HMS Beagle (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 24.1).
